routes.name: Long Term Entry Permit (on an Immigrant Employment Certificate)

note: St Helena, read on the St Helena Government's immigration pages (sainthelena.gov.sh) on 2026-10-30; Ascension's and Tristan da Cunha's own immigration rules aren't read. An employer needs an Immigrant Employment Certificate (one to five years, a fee charged but not stated) to employ an immigrant, and each such employee must hold a Long Term Entry Permit (issued for at most five years, the term kept) and pass the points-based system: work for the sponsor. Working self-employed beyond six months takes a Work Permit from the Immigration Control Board alongside a Long Term Entry Permit (a fee charged, not stated); an extension of up to five years may be granted (read as a five-year term, renewable). Where either is applied for isn't stated ('either' is the game's reading). St Helenian status is granted to one of good character, intending St Helena as their home, who was in St Helena at the start of the five years before applying and meets the time-spent requirement (three years for a St Helenian's spouse); it is read as the permanent route, applied for in St Helena. No fee or decision time is on the pages; how many days the time-spent requirement allows isn't stated, so no years to it are kept.

sources.title: St Helena Government, Immigrant Employment Certificate
sources.said: An Immigrant Employment Certificate is required by an employer to employ immigrants in St Helena and can be valid for a period of one to five years. ... A fee is chargeable ... Each immigrant employee must hold a Long Term Entry Permit and pass Points Based System

sources.title: St Helena Government, Long Term Entry Permit
sources.said: The Long-term Entry Permit is issuable for a period not exceeding five years.

sources.title: St Helena Government, Work Permits
sources.said: A Work Permit is required to work on a self-employed basis in St. Helena for a period in excess of six months. It does not allow entry to St. Helena. A Long Term Entry Permit is required for entry to St. Helena. ... An extension of up to five years may be granted if the above conditions are met and the application is made three months before the expiry of the current Work Permit.

sources.title: St Helena Government, St Helenian Status
sources.said: St Helenian status can either be acquired by right or by grant (through application). ... Intends, in the event of a certificate being granted to him, that his home or his principal home will be in St Helena ... Was in St Helena at the beginning of period of five years ending with date of application ... Meets the requirement in relation to time spent in St Helena
